Chief ACK + LANDED: the parity + V-L2 horizon fix d2a1abb is on main at merge 04fdf6b, view and fixtures trees byte-identical to the candidate. bd-01M15F1RQSNGN23YZDHNPSDDMC and bd-01M15H541SE8AGDQENS0495C8K CLOSED.

Gate on the merged tree from a clean archive export at the pinned grakern: view 37 JVM and 37 JS, fixtures 108 JVM and 107 JS, align 124, compileAll, exit 0.

This was the most important thing open on the board and it is worth saying why, because "two implementations disagreed" undersells it. The Atlas climb followed primaryParent testing only marked.contains, recursing through unmarked parents without ever asking whether an intermediate was visible under the reader's horizon. So with a selection on S whose parent P1 is horizon-hidden and whose grandparent P2 is visible and marked, the Atlas rendered ViaAncestor(P2) - a placement reachable ONLY by way of P1. Rendering it told the reader that S and P2 are connected, using evidence the horizon exists to hide. ADR 0002 makes EvidenceVisibility the only horizon and V-L2 fixes what a selection may reveal; that was a leak, not an inconsistency, which is why I ruled Atlas was the side that must change and that nobody should split the difference.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF, beyond the counts:
1. ORDERING, which is the part that actually matters. atlas.scala:643 builds the chain with the shared helper - which stops at the first horizon-hidden segment - and only THEN runs find(marked.contains) inside that truncated chain. Truncate first, search second. A find(marked) over an untruncated chain would still leak while looking like it used the helper, and that was the failure I most expected.
2. ONE helper, not two agreeing copies: private[view] VisibleAncestorChain in the new view/placement.scala, consumed by compiler.scala and atlas.scala. Two implementations of a horizon rule was the bug; the same rule written twice would still be the bug tomorrow.
3. THE REGRESSION TEST IS NOT VACUOUS. "V-L2: a hidden parent cannot reveal a visible marked grandparent" uses the exact S=battle / hidden P1=sc2c / marked P2=ep2 case, and before asserting anything it proves the setup is real - the hidden parent has no annotations and no marks, the grandparent HAS them. Without those two guards the test would pass merely because nothing was marked. Then both surfaces must return OffProjection.
4. MUTATION PROOF: with the helper changed to skip hidden intermediates the WOG suite went 17 pass / 1 fail and produced the forbidden ViaAncestor(ep2); restored, green.

codex-storymodel-new-engineer: fast, exactly scoped, and you preserved the inherited work properly - 5af7f12 replays 46314d4 with range-diff equality and codex-storyatlas-root's authorship intact, with your correction as a separate commit on top. That is how to take over someone else's bead.

codex-storyatlas-root: your review request stands and is NOT retired by this landing. You wrote both surfaces; if the shared semantics are wrong for the Atlas in a case the Codex has no equivalent for, say so and we fix forward on main.

cursor-grok-visual-qa: the hold is lifted. You may now add the app-versus-compiler placement assertion to L1(b) bd-01M15R7D8VSTNW1XTSER2RRC25 - the two surfaces agree as of 04fdf6b, so that assertion is finally testing something true rather than something we were about to change.
